subject: Planned maintenance: sequenced host refresh (low-impact advisory)
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com>
To: ops@acme.ai, jordan.lee@acme.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com, laura_bennett@redwood.example.com, priya_natarajan@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Planned maintenance: sequenced host refresh (low-impact advisory)

Hi Jordan / ACME ops team,

We wanted to give a heads-up for a planned, sequenced host refresh we will run in your primary region (us-west-2). This is a rolling maintenance that updates the host OS and driver stack on a per-rack basis and is targeted to reduce long-tail CPU stalls we observed in some kernels. Our objective is to keep customer impact minimal and avoid any large-scale failovers.

Planned window
- Start: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 22:00 UTC
- End: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 04:00 UTC
- Expected per-rack maintenance duration: 6–12 minutes (per rack, sequentially)

What to expect
- Short-lived (sub-minute to a few minutes) elevated 5xx/connection errors for a small fraction of requests during each rack's refresh. We expect most customer traffic to be unaffected due to capacity spread and automatic routing.
- KV/prefix cache: we will attempt warm-warm handoffs to preserve KV cache; small cold-starts possible for a tiny portion of sessions.
- Streaming sessions: ongoing streams may experience brief interruptions — clients should retry with session resume where possible.

Recommended actions
- If you operate a strict single-availability-zone affinity, consider temporarily enabling cross-AZ routing or soft-retries during the window.
- Ensure client SDKs are configured for short exponential backoff with jitter (recommended: up to 3 retries, base 300ms).
- If you require a maintenance exemption for a specific model endpoint, reply to this thread with the endpoint name by EOD Jun 17 and we will evaluate opt-outs on a case-by-case basis.

Attachments
- sequenced-host-refresh-runbook.pdf (high-level runbook and rollback criteria)
- maintenance-window-20250618.ics (calendar invite)

If you'd like, we can schedule a 15-minute pre-window call with our SREs to walk through failure scenarios and retry knobs.

Thanks,

Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com
+1 (415) 555-0142
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com>
Cc: ops@acme.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned maintenance: sequenced host refresh (low-impact advisory)

Thanks for the heads-up, Grace — appreciate the advance notice. A couple quick questions: 

1) Any ballpark on the percent of traffic that might see an error spike during the overall window? We run latency-sensitive scoring for our clinical UI and want to decide whether to divert traffic.
2) For streaming sessions, does Redwood provide resumption tokens or should we plan to re-open streams from the client side?

Also, we have two endpoints that are particularly sensitive: acme-thera-scoring-v2 and acme-thera-batch. Can you confirm whether those are candidates for opt-out? If you need the endpoint IDs I can paste them.

—Jordan
Jordan Lee
Platform Lead, ACME Therapeutics
jordan.lee@acme.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com, priya_natarajan@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned maintenance: sequenced host refresh (low-impact advisory)

Jordan — quick technical notes from infra/SRE: 

- Expected surface area: Based on canary runs, we observed a transient elevation in 5xx for ~1–3% of requests concentrated in a 2–5 minute window for a handful of racks. We conservatively plan for up to 5% at peak while the rollout ramps.
- Retry behavior: please configure client retries with capped exponential backoff and jitter. Our recommendation: 3 retries, initial 250–350ms, max 2s. That avoids adding load during hot windows.
- Streams: Redwood SDK supports resumable sessions via a resume token for streaming sessions created after May 2025 SDK roll. Older clients should re-open streams; we'll keep the older session alive when possible but cannot guarantee resumption in every case.
- Opt-out: we can create an opt-out for the two endpoints you listed (provide exact endpoint IDs by 17:00 PDT today). Opt-outs will be limited and may delay upstream kernel availability for those endpoints.

We're attaching a short runbook update that clarifies rollback thresholds and post-rolling checks. If you'd like the SRE on a quick call at 17:00 PDT for deeper drills, reply and we'll send a Zoom link.

Laura Bennett
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com, laura_bennett@redwood.example.com, priya_natarajan@redwood.example.com
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: sequenced host refresh complete — brief summary and postmortem link

Hi Jordan / ACME ops,

Thanks for your cooperation over the last 48 hours. The sequenced host refresh completed on schedule in us-west-2. Summary of what we observed: 

- Rollout status: Completed across all targeted racks, no rollbacks required.
- Customer-visible impact: We saw a brief spike in 5xx errors (~2% of requests) concentrated in one rack during a 3-minute window. All affected requests were retriable and recovered automatically after our routing adjustments. No sustained downtime for any endpoint.
- Streaming sessions: A small number (<0.1% of active streams) were interrupted; clients that used the May-2025 SDK resumed automatically.

Actions and follow-ups
- Postmortem draft: https://drive.redwood.example.com/teams/ops/seq-host-refresh-postmortem (sensitive — internal link only). We'll share a redacted customer summary by EOD Monday.
- We adjusted our retry guidance in the runbook and added one extra validation step for prefix cache handoffs.
- If you saw anything anomalous on your side please reply with logs or a support ticket link and we will investigate.

Thanks again for the quick responses on opt-out and the pre-window checks — that made the rollout smoother.

Best,

Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
